**Finding: missing (critical) — no ownership / IP clause in the Agreement.**

What I checked:
- **sec-p0001 / sec-1.4** (HDI's and Company's responsibilities, fees, term, Site management) — HDI designs, develops, hosts and bears all build costs; the Company supplies "Content" (2.1) and has exclusive artistic and editorial control (5.2); title language at 5.3 covers only physical Deerskin Products, not IP.
- **sec-5.4** (exclusivity, cross-promotions, confidentiality, warranties, general provisions) — only IP-adjacent items are the limited, non-exclusive licence of the Company's "Marks" to HDI (6.1), the reciprocal e-mail list cross-promotion (7.1), and confidentiality (8). The "co-ownership" reference in 10.2 is a no-partnership disclaimer, not an IP allocation.
- Searches for "Proprietary Rights", "intellectual property", "own", and a definition of "Content" confirm there is no ownership, assignment, work-product or Customer Data provision anywhere.

Why it matters: nothing states who owns the Site deliverables HDI builds, the Content we supply, our Marks beyond the narrow licence, or the customer/user/order data the Site generates — leaving HDI, as developer and host, in a position to claim them.

Redline (validated, ok:true) — new **5.5 Proprietary Rights** inserted after p0035: Company owns Content, Marks and Company Data; HDI assigns Site Deliverables but retains its pre-existing platform/tools with a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence back to us; no assignment of Company IP/data to HDI and no joint ownership. Because HDI funds the build, the comment offers the playbook fallback (perpetual licence to use, modify and sublicense the Deliverables in lieu of assignment) as a landing zone, while holding firm on Content and Company Data ownership.
